definition.note: No closed form is stored for this surface. It is defined by its shipped implementation in math_art.minsurf.parametric, which is authoritative; an unverified transcription would silently define a different surface.

provenance.definition: Derived from the Math Art generator registries and cross-referenced to the literature; not transcribed from any gallery's compilation.
sources: M. J. Callahan, D. Hoffman, W. H. Meeks III, "Embedded minimal surfaces with an infinite number of ends", Invent. Math. 96 (1989) 459-505;
C. J. Costa (1984); D. Hoffman, W. H. Meeks III (1985); M. Weber, https://minimalsurfaces.blog/ -- the harvested notebooks (research/msblog_harvest/singly_periodic.json).
H. Karcher, "Embedded minimal surfaces derived from Scherk's examples", Manuscripta Math. 62 (1988) 83-114;

cross_checked.detail: UNRESOLVED between three statements, so no genus is asserted here: (a) the page's convention 'denote by CHM_r,s a translation invariant surface with 2r ends of genus s+1 in the quotient' makes CHM-(1,2) genus 3 with 2 ends; (b) the shipped implementation (math_art/minsurf/zoo.py) measures quotient genus 4 with 2 planar ends (chi = -8); (c) Invent. Math. 96 (1989) covers only the dihedral family M_k (genus 2k+1), of which CHM-(1,2) is not a member.  Note the same page convention gives CHM-(1,1) genus 2, which contradicts the 1989 paper's genus 3 for M_1 -- so the blog's genus convention appears shifted by one, and the record's name '(genus 4)' agrees with the measurement.  Flagged for resolution against Weber's 'CHM 1999' manuscript.
